title: Undoer of knots
hookLine: a painting in Augsburg shows Mary untying a knotted ribbon, and the devotion travels with Pope Francis

cards: Above an altar in a church in Augsburg, in Germany, hangs a painting. Mary stands in the middle, with angels around her.
On one side, an angel hands her a long white ribbon full of knots, and her hands are busy, working one loose. On the other side, another angel carries the ribbon away, smooth.
That's the whole drama: a woman patiently untying knots. Yesterday's line from Irenaeus has a face. Today's word: undoer of knots.

teach.b: Tradition links the picture to Irenaeus's knot: what Eve's disobedience tied, Mary's obedience loosened. The canvas gives an ancient bishop's sentence a ribbon and a pair of hands.

In the devotion that grew around the painting, the knots are the tangles of a life: a marriage in trouble, a family that won't speak, a habit that won't let go, a fear wound so tight there's no loose end to pull.
People bring their own knot to Mary and ask her to pray for them, that with God's grace it may work loose. Then how it traveled.

The story goes that a young Jesuit from Argentina, Jorge Mario Bergoglio, came across the image while studying in Germany. Back in Buenos Aires, he gave out cards with the picture, and a devotion took root there.
He later became Pope Francis. And the patience in it. Look at Mary's hands.
She isn't slashing the ribbon with a knife. A knot pulled hard gets tighter.
A knot worked slowly, a little this way and a little that, gives.

That's one picture of how grace can work: not all at once, but loop by loop. In Catholic teaching Mary doesn't replace God here. She prays, as a mother would, and God does the untying through her prayer.

how: Catholics who keep this devotion pray before copies of the Augsburg image, often with the rosary or a novena, naming a particular trouble.

games.q: a knot in a ribbon is stuck. what does the painting show Mary doing?
games.why: her hands work the knot loose. pulled hard, a knot tightens; worked slowly, it gives.

practice: Let one knot in your life come to mind, just one, and look at it honestly: where it's tight, and what keeps pulling it tighter.
Then imagine handing that stretch of ribbon to someone with patient hands; you don't have to see how it comes undone.
If you pray, ask Mary, undoer of knots, to pray for you with the words of the Hail Mary; if you don't, simply loosen your grip a little.

wordCard.voice: Undoer of knots. A title for Mary from a painting in Augsburg. This week's road: the cost is the point, conscience at the checkout, love made structural, four teachings, ever virgin, the knot untied, and now she undoes knots.

carryVoice: Your line: she undoes knots. Not cut, but worked loose, loop by loop. Gently, until tomorrow.
